fields.mechanism: Excessive no-load current caused by high core losses or rotor drag, consistent with the power analysis of a 3-phase induction motor drive conveyor, generates sufficient I²R heating in the stator windings to trip the thermal overload despite balanced winding resistance and stable 400V supply.
fields.intervention: Perform a no-load current measurement per phase and compare against the motor nameplate no-load current specification; if elevated, disassemble the motor to inspect for degraded stator lamination insulation (increasing eddy current core losses) or bearing degradation causing mechanical rotor drag.
fields.expected_effect: Identifying and rectifying the source of excessive no-load current will reduce stator winding heat generation, preventing the thermal overload from tripping during 20 minutes of no-load operation while maintaining balanced resistance and stable voltage.
fields.falsification_test: Measure the no-load line current on all three phases with a true-RMS clamp meter; if the measured no-load current is within 10 percent of the manufacturer specified no-load current and the motor still trips the thermal overload within 20 minutes, this mechanism is falsified.
